filename: Structured Exploration of Machine Learning Model  Complexity for Spatio-Temporal Forecasting of Urban Flooding.pdf
title: Structured exploration of machine learning model complexity for spatio-temporal forecasting of urban flooding
code_availability: The processed data and the codes used in this study are available from the corresponding authors upon reasonable request.
testbed_rationale: The focus is urban flood forecasting using crowdsourced municipal complaints and radar/gauge precipitation rather than Earth system model parameterization or physical process emulation.
pain_points: Unavailability of detailed urban drainage and sewer network maps prevents physical hydrodynamic modeling
Crowdsourced 311 complaint data contains inherent human reporting and commuter biases and is less precise than direct physical sensor measurements
Sparse response data in certain low-reporting zones degrades neural network predictive capability
Brief temporal duration of flash flood events limits the utility of standard temporal sequence models without graph/spatial connections
extraction_notes: Discussion paper preprint published under EGUsphere. Authored by researchers associated with the NSF LEAP Center at Columbia University.
